## TL;DR

The Stories, Inbox and Search pages were checked with 200+ item fixtures, long and unbroken titles, and zero-result states at 375, 768 and 1280 px. One real defect was found and fixed: on the phone work queue, the Priority, Area and Story filters shared a horizontal scroller, so the Area select was cut off mid-label and the Story select sat off the right edge with no cue that it existed. The filter row now wraps. The regression test was tightened so it would have caught this: the earlier audit excluded every scroller, which hid the bug. The test now checks each control against its clipping ancestors, asserts the phone filters are in view, and resolves every internal link against the real router. All 18 cases pass, and `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check` is green. Real devices, the dark theme and live data were not checked.

## Work and rationale

I picked up from a previous turn that had written a 670-line Playwright test and had not yet run it. The test mounts the real `StoriesView`, `WorkView`, `MobileWorkQueue` and `SearchOverlay` in jsdom with seeded stores, serializes the markup, and injects it into headless WebKit with the built global stylesheet and scoped CSS compiled from the current SFC sources. Component CSS comes from source; only the global stylesheet is read from `dist/ui`.

The first run passed. Passing on the first run was not enough, so I rebuilt the UI and took screenshots (`QA_SHOTS`) and read the fold shots at 375 px. The phone inbox queue showed the Area select as "Any a" at the right edge, and the empty-project state showed the same clip. The Story select was not visible at all. The audit had not caught this because it excluded every horizontal scroller wholesale. I changed the audit so each visible button, link, select and input must be fully inside every clipping ancestor, and I added an explicit assertion that the Area and Story selects are in view at 375 px.

The fix is a one-line design change in `MobileWorkQueue.vue`: `.mobile-chip-row` changed from `overflow-x: auto` to `flex-wrap: wrap`. A scroller hides controls with no affordance, and at phone width a wrapped row is better than a hidden one. I ran a red check to confirm the new assertions are real: with the old scrolling CSS restored, the phone inbox case failed with `clips a control`. Then I restored the fix and the case passed.

The new control check also flagged the story drawer's close button as clipped by the Vue mount container. The drawer is `position: fixed`, so no ancestor's scroll box clips it, and the screenshot shows the × fully visible. I made the walk stop at a fixed box rather than suppress the check, so the rule still applies to every static ancestor.

The dead-link check is the one part I could not make bite. The app router sends unknown paths to `/` through a catch-all, so a dead link would redirect quietly. The check resolves each internal `href` against the real router and rejects the catch-all match. No dead links were found on the audited pages, but the check now runs on every case.

The QA doc is `docs/qa/2026-11-stories-inbox-search-qa.md`. A previous WIP commit on this branch (`f4cc4f151`) already contained a version of it that concluded there were no product defects and called the phone chip strip an intentional scroll region. That conclusion was wrong, so I corrected the committed doc in place rather than replacing it wholesale. I first overwrote it by mistake while drafting. I restored the committed version from git before editing, and kept the parts that are still accurate: the empty-state copy, the router links, the copy-link chips and the harness note about scope-id matching.

## Approaches tried

- **Trusting the existing audit.** Tried first: the first run passed on the unfixed page. The scroller exclusion was the blind spot, not evidence of a clean page.
- **Allow-listing the close button.** Considered and rejected. A fixed-box rule is a general fact about clipping; an allow-list would hide the next real clip.
- **Keeping the scroller with a scroll cue versus wrapping.** Considered; I chose wrap. A cue still hides the Story filter behind a gesture, and the row has only three filters, so wrapping costs a few pixels of height. I did not try the cue.
- **Matching `href`s against a hard-coded route list.** Considered and not used. Resolving against the real router is more accurate and cannot drift from the route table.

## Challenges and blockers

- The test is WebKit-only and runs through the UI vitest config; the root `vitest` invocation fails at import because it does not load the Vue plugin. The repo's `bun run test` wrapper handles this, and `repoos check` runs the suite correctly.
- The first doc edit used a whole-file Write that overwrote a committed file I had not read. I restored it from git before any further change, and the final doc diff is the corrected version, not my draft.
- Coverage is partial by design. The phone-only states (paged queue, no-match, empty) run only at 375 px because they use the narrow layout. The inbox board runs only at 768 and 1280 px because it uses the desktop layout. The zero-stories and all-complete states run at 375 and 1280. The table in the doc shows this.
- The previous handoff failed at the commit step: git could not create `index.lock` under the main checkout's worktree admin directory. When I looked again the lock was gone and no git process was running, so I did not touch it. I re-ran the scoped gate and the 18 cases on the unchanged branch; both pass.
- The scoped gate skipped its test step because `REPOOS_SKIP_TESTS=1` is set in this environment. I ran the new test file directly with `bun run test -- stories-inbox-search-qa` instead.
- I did not declare `--shots`. A desktop capture cannot show the phone-only filter row, and this change has no desktop-visible effect to show.
- One visual observation was not investigated: the "Hide Completed Stories" checkbox sits on its own line in the all-complete state at 375 px. The markup is the same in both states, so this is likely the checked-state styling. It is listed in the doc as unverified.

## Key learnings

- A scroller in an audit is a hiding place. Excluding scrollers wholesale made the audit pass on exactly the defect it was meant to find. The right rule checks what a reader can reach, not what is inside the viewport.
- A dead link in a SPA with a catch-all route does not 404. Checking that a link resolves to a real route, rather than to the fallback, is the only reliable check.
- Fixed-position drawers escape ancestor clipping. A clipping check has to know that, or it reports phantom clips on every drawer.
- Verify a red check before trusting a green one. Component scoped CSS is compiled from source at test time, so rebuilding `dist/` does not change it. A red check means temporarily restoring the old source CSS, which is what I did for the phone filter row.
